messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: High token billing spike detected for tenant aurora-123 (dedicated:vpc-aurora-1). Alert triggered by billing-anomaly-runner. Current 5m token rate = 7.2x baseline. Severity: P1

maria (oncall): acked — looking. can someone pull the token distribution and confirm it's not a billing exporter flail?

nina-sre: on it — pulling per-tenant token histogram now. initial query shows median tokens/request up from ~120 -> ~850 for aurora-123 over last 20m.

kevin-se: adding context from SE — Aurora recently rolled a client-side SDK update that normalizes text differently (they switched to NFC). if their client is tokenizing differently than our runtime tokenizer that could inflate counts. any recent model changes in dedicated pool?

maria (oncall): no model swaps reported in audits for vpc-aurora-1. eng-runtime-bot, did any tokenizer deploys or config changes hit that pool in last 24h?

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy log check: no tokenizer microservice deploys in prod for vpc-aurora-1 in last 24h. There was a config push to routing rules 36h ago (no tokenizer changes).

jack-cs: contacting Aurora account — letting them know we're investigating. they report customers started seeing sudden billing increases and 429s for heavy requests.

liz-ps: quick ask — is tenant isolation holding? We must ensure other tenants in same pool unaffected to avoid broader mitigation.

nina-sre: isolation check: checked top-10 tenants in vpc-aurora-1 — only aurora-123 shows token spike. network/CPU/queue latencies normal. suggests tokenizer mismatch on input stream rather than runtime perf regression.

kevin-se: likely root cause hypothesis: client-side normalization -> different byte sequences (emoji ZWJ clusters, NFKC/NFC) -> our byte-level-bpe tokenizer splits differently -> token counts multiplied. I've seen similar with zero-width joiners and foreign diacritics.

maria (oncall): need quick mitigations: 1) stop further billing surprise for Aurora 2) reduce 429s for their customers 3) get a patch that normalizes input on our side and roll it with minimal risk. proposals?

kevin-se: short-term: apply per-tenant soft token cap and switch billing to pre-normalized token estimate (so we don't bill 7x while we triage). Medium-term: server-side normalize to NFKC before tokenization and deploy to tokenizer service. Long-term: publish client SDK guidance and add an option to runtime to accept client-reported tokenizer mode (but must be opted-in).

maria (oncall): admin action I can take now: apply quota cap and enable provisional billing override for aurora-123. does anyone disagree?

jack-cs: do it. Aurora will prefer a billing cap while we remediate. i told them we can pause billing on anomalous requests.

maria (oncall): applying soft cap 1.5k tokens/request for aurora-123 and enabling estimated billing fallback. command: 

```
# internal admin CLI
redwood-admin tenants set-limit --tenant aurora-123 --type soft-token-cap --value 1500 --until 1818240000
redwood-admin billing override --tenant aurora-123 --mode estimated --note "anomaly mitigation"
```

maria (oncall): cap applied and billing override enabled. monitoring for 5m.

eng-runtime-bot: routing note: requests > cap are now truncated with a 429-with-hint header and not billed beyond cap while override active.

nina-sre: pushed a non-invasive normalization transform behind feature-flag to tokenizer-staging and smoke-tested against a sample of aurora payloads (emoji/ZWJ/diacritics). results: token counts align with Aurora's client-side expected counts in ~95% of cases.

kevin-se: share the test snippet please — we need to review for edgecases (e.g., CJK and mixed scripts).

nina-sre: test snippet: 
```
# normalize to NFKC then token_count
from unicodedata import normalize
s = normalize('NFKC', input_text)
# then feed to byte-level tokenizer
```

kevin-se: looks right. potential risk: normalization can change semantic for signed legal text where characters matter. confirm with legal/compliance? but for now Aurora ok to proceed.

jack-cs: Aurora approves server-side normalization for their tenant only (they confirmed it's safe for their workload). green light from customer.

maria (oncall): plan: 1) enable tenant-scoped NFKC normalization feature-flag for aurora-123 in tokenizer service 2) monitor token counts and billing for 30m 3) after stability, roll to prod cluster for tenant. who owns deployment?

nina-sre: i'll own the feature-flag toggle and rollout. will only affect aurora-123 routing shard. deployment steps below.

```
# staging -> canary -> prod toggle
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/tokenizer FEATURE_NORMALIZE_NFKC=aurora-123
kubectl -n infra rollout status deploy/tokenizer
# validate on canary pod
curl -s -H "X-Tenant: aurora-123" https://tokenizer.internal/normalize-test | jq .token_count
```

nina-sre: canary passed. enabling in prod shard for vpc-aurora-1 now.

deploy-bot: rollout started for tokenizer feature flag (pairing to shards: vpc-aurora-1 -> shard-3).

maria (oncall): monitoring. graphs show median tokens/request for aurora-123 falling from 850 -> 140 over 6 minutes. billing estimate trending back to baseline.

jack-cs: telling Aurora it's fixed on our side. they reported a handful of customers still seeing high counts (old cached SDK). advising them to update.

kevin-se: follow-up: we'll add a normalization compatibility test to onboarding for VPC tenants and a note in Dedicated docs. also recommend we add a per-tenant tokenizer-mode header so clients can signal expected normalization in future.

liz-ps: isolation confirmed — no collateral impact. good job.

maria (oncall): severity -> S2. paging muted. leaving handoff to nina for follow-ups and postmortem. nina, you oncall for next 6h?

nina-sre: taking handoff. I'll keep the flag enabled for 24h, coordinate with engineering for a targeted postmortem and ensure billing reconciles with Aurora.

jack-cs: will coordinate invoice adjustments and confirm customer satisfaction.

eng-runtime-bot: incident summary stub: tenant aurora-123 tokenization mismatch due to client normalization mismatch. Mitigations: billing override, soft token cap, tenant-scoped NFKC normalization toggle. Status: mitigated. Assigned -> nina-sre for follow-up.

maria (oncall): thanks team :thumbsup: — closing active page. please add any notes to the postmortem doc and include sample payloads, tokenizer diffs, and commands used.

nina-sre: will open postmortem and include the exact regexes and normalization code. putting a link here once created.

deploy-bot: incident page closed by maria (oncall).
